question_text: According to the course material, negotiation is a dialogue intended to produce an agreement upon courses of action, to bargain for individual or collective advantage, to resolve disputes or to craft outcomes to satisfy various interests; it is the primary method of:
explanation: Negotiation is the primary method of alternative dispute resolution.

question_text: According to the course material, negotiation occurs in business, non-profit organisations, government branches, legal proceedings, among nations and in personal situations such as employment salary, marriage, divorce and:
explanation: Negotiation occurs in many settings including everyday life. The study is negotiation theory.

question_text: According to the course material, professional negotiators are often specialized, such as union negotiators, leverage buyout negotiators, peace negotiators, hostage negotiators, or may work under other titles such as diplomats, legislators or:
explanation: Specialized negotiators include diplomats, legislators or brokers.

question_text: According to the course material, before reaching a negotiation stage of selling the business, a vendor should ensure his company is totally ready for a sale and any of the potential purchasers must have carried out:
explanation: Due diligence is invaluable during any negotiation process.

question_text: According to the course material, a common tactic is for a purchaser to try and understand the aspiration of a vendor; most people become emotionally attached to business and could have personal friends within staff; understanding this is a very important tool for:
explanation: Basic psychology: understand the vendor's emotional attachment and staff friendships.

question_text: According to the course material, while preparing for an important negotiation be sure to invest time to answer what the other team's hot buttons are, what they hope to achieve at company, group and personal level, and who are all:
explanation: Prepare: hot buttons, hoped-for achievements, needs, interested parties.

question_text: According to the course material, according to Cees van Riel and Charles Fombrun in Essentials of Corporate Communication, corporate communication is the set of activities involved in managing and orchestrating all internal and external communications aimed at creating favorable starting points with stakeholders on which:
explanation: Van Riel and Fombrun: orchestrating internal and external communications for favorable starting points with stakeholders.

question_text: According to the course material, Jackson (1987) remarks that it is corporate communication without a final s; he left communications to the telecommunications specialists, tired of being called on to fix the company switchboard or recommend:
explanation: Jackson adopted 'corporate communication' without a final s for clarity.

question_text: According to the course material, corporate communication encodes and promotes a strong corporate culture, coherent corporate identity, reasonable corporate philosophy, genuine sense of corporate citizenship, an appropriate relationship with the press including quick responsible ways of communicating in a crisis, understanding of communication tools and technologies, and sophisticated approaches to:
explanation: Also managing perceptions: timely information, positive image, smooth relationships with all stakeholders.

question_text: According to the course material, gone are the days when corporate communication merely meant wining and dining the client; it has now emerged as a science and art of:
explanation: Reputation management has gained importance; corporate communication is perception management.

question_text: According to the course material, corporate communication is issued by a corporate organisation to all its publics; internal publics include employees and stakeholders such as share and stock holders, while external publics include agencies, channel partners, media, government, industry bodies, educational institutes and:
option_c: only a finder of a GSM
explanation: Publics: internal (employees, shareholders) and external (media, government, general public).

question_text: According to the course material, the interview is perhaps the most nerve-wracking aspect of the recruitment process, not just for the candidate but also for the interviewer; if conducted competently it is a useful opportunity for a candidate to prove he or she will be an asset and for an employer to promote the organisation and therefore:
explanation: A competent interview helps both sides: prove the candidate is an asset and attract the best employees.

question_text: According to the course material, given that people are the most important resource in any organisation, recruiting the wrong ones can be costly; in fact replacing an employee can cost up to:
option_a: 50 percent of that employee's annual salary
explanation: Replacing an employee can cost up to 50 percent of that employee's annual salary. (Guide typesets it as 5opercent.)

question_text: According to the course material, the interview is essentially a meeting to put the proverbial flesh on the bones of information provided by a candidate on their application form or CV; your purpose is to satisfy yourself that the candidate meets the requirement for the job and fits in with:
explanation: Satisfy yourself the candidate meets job requirements and fits the culture.

question_text: According to the course material, effective interview questions come from knowing what skills and attitudes a job requires; you should have already defined the job criteria before advertising a position, and scan CVs for points including whether there is an unexplained gap in:
explanation: Note achievements and any unexplained employment-history gap.

question_text: According to the course material, we are living in a jet age and a world that can now be described as a global village; information is sent across the world in a twinkle of an eye, and the level of technology at a business's disposal will determine:
option_a: the extent of success of the business
explanation: Technology available determines the extent of business success.

question_text: According to the course material, communication technology provides access to information and markets, connects people to marketing opportunities, causes efficiency in transaction activities, and the computer-mediated communication technology includes conferencing technologies and:
explanation: Computer-mediated: conferencing technologies and messaging systems; also facilitates group work.

question_text: According to the course material, communication technology helps to develop thinking skills, decrease the need for memorisation of the facts, evaluate current information and develop:
explanation: Thinking skills, less memorisation, evaluate current information, accessing skills. Also helps train workers.

question_text: According to the course material, the popular communication technologies are teleconference, telephone, e-mail, fax and:
explanation: Teleconference, telephone, e-mail, fax, Internet.

question_text: According to the course material, a teleconference or teleseminar is the live exchange and mass articulation of information among several persons and machines remote from one another but linked by:
explanation: Linked by a telecommunications system. Also called audio/telephone/phone conferencing.

question_text: According to the course material, the first and foremost difficulty in telephoning is not being able to see the person you are communicating with; this lack of visual communication often makes users nervous and thereby hinders their communicative abilities, added to the typical hectic pace of:
explanation: No visual channel plus hectic pace makes telephoning particularly difficult.

question_text: According to the course material, Module 4 of BUS207 is the final module and contains negotiation skills, corporate communication, interview skills and:
explanation: Module 4: negotiation, corporate communication, interview skills, communication technology.

question_text: According to the course material, organisations can strategically communicate to their audiences through public relations and advertising; this may involve an employee newsletter or video, crisis management with the news media, special events planning, building product value and communicating with stockholders, clients or:
option_b: only a finder of a GSM
explanation: PR and advertising: newsletters, crisis management, events, product value, stockholders/clients/donors.

question_text: According to the course material, there are sixteen study units in BUS207 divided into four modules of four units each, and the package is made of 16 study units and:
explanation: 16 study units in 4 modules of 4 units each, plus a course guide.

question_text: According to the course material, the course writers of BUS207 are Mrs. Eunice Adegbola, with content editor Dr. (Mrs) Rahila Gowon of the Directorate of General Studies, University of Jos, and Head of Department of Administration:
explanation: Writer: Mrs. Eunice Adegbola. Editor: Dr. Rahila Gowon. HOD: Dr. Yemisi I. Ogunlela. Coordinator: Mrs. Ihuoma Ikemba-Efughi.
